title: Check and Double Check: dark makeup for Tizol and Bigard
summary: They were made up darker for the film and gave them cold cream; Bing Crosby sang Three Little Words.

blocks.x: But they usually did those on sound-stages, though. Then 'Check and Doublecheck,' 1930, 'a comedy vehicle for Amos and Andy playing a well-meaning pair having trouble over a deed to property. Duke Ellington and his orchestra are featured in a ballroom sequence, playing 'Three Little Words,' and 'Old Man Blues.' Freddie Jenkins, Cootie

Williams, Arthur Whetsol, Joe Nanton, Juan Tizol, Barney Bigard, Johnny Hodges, Harry Carney, Fred Guy, Wellman Braud, Sonny Greer, Ellington. Tizol and Bigard are suitably blacked up for the occasion; the song, Ring Dem Bells, is also used. ""
Do you remember that, when they made you put dark makeup on?
Oh, they put makeup for everybody.
But this says they made you and Barney a lot darker.
And they gave us the cold cream and so forth, when we got through, to go there and wash it off and take all that stuff off. Oh, it was awful.
That was for "Check and Doublecheck." Do you remember anything else about Check and Doublecheck? ""

Bing Crosby sang Three Little Words with the three Kings, you know? Remember that trio that Bing Crosby used to sing with years and years ago. What did they call themselves? The Three Rhythm Kings, or something.
The three fellows, they recorded Three Little Words. ""
